ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute: the $5.00 cancellation fee stands (NS-1 satisfied — driver_tap at 12:17:10, 39 m from pickup, 490 s continuous within 200 m until cancellation); no refund, no account action.
ruling.reasoning:
The case arrives as a driver-cancelled trip (cancelled_by = driver, F4), so it enters the policy through NS-0, which routes a driver cancellation claiming passenger no-show to NS-1/NS-2 [F4][NS-0]. The record's no-show threshold is 8 minutes and the fee on the record is $5.00, and the trace reads those figures wherever NS-1/NS-2 say 3 minutes / $6.61 [F4][F7][NS-1].

NS-1 (i) is met: arrival was confirmed by the driver's own tap, not by a platform auto-judgement — "driver_tap at 12:17:10" [F6][NS-1]. NS-1 (ii) is met: at the moment of that tap the GPS placed the car 39 m from the pickup point, inside the 200 m data-layer radius, and the closest approach overall was 6 m at 12:16:45 [F6][F1][NS-1].

NS-1 (iii) is met: the trace records 490 s continuously inside the 200 m radius after the tap against the 480 s threshold, and the GPS shows the car stationary from 12:16:50 to the 12:25:20 cancellation, 41 m from the pickup [F6][F3][NS-1]. The GPS and timeline also cover the whole wait with no hole beyond the hole threshold, so the completeness proviso in NS-1 does not send the wait finding to human review [F2][F6][NS-1]; the chat is likewise complete and fully timestamped, two of two messages [F11][NS-1].

The driver's invocation of "the full 8 minutes the rule gives" does not undo this: under NS-1 the record's 8-minute threshold governs, and the measured post-tap wait of 490 s and the arrival-to-cancellation gap of 9 min 55 s both reach it, so the driver's matching count applied is the correct one rather than a substituted free-wait figure [F6][F5][F10][F12][NS-1]. The driver's notice of arrival at 12:17 and his cancellation message at 12:25 are consistent with that clock [F9][F10][NS-1].

No NS-2 ground exists, because no NS-1 element fails: the tap was made, its position was inside the radius, and the wait inside the radius exceeded the threshold [F6][F3][NS-2]. No traffic or weather fact supplies a competing explanation for the timeline — band 3 on LORONG AH SOO, no incidents near the route, fair weather — but that simply confirms an unobstructed pickup at which the rider did not board, not a reroute justification the driver ever relied on [F13][F14][F15][NS-1].

The $5.00 line is the fee the record attaches to that cancellation; NS-1's predicate is made out and, with no surge applied, the FARE-1 screen surfaces no unpublished or unsupported add-on to strip out [F7][F8][NS-1]. On the evidence the driver's side offers the rule the record requires, the completed facts show the rider was not there when the car was waiting [F3][F5][F6][NS-1].

NS-7 keeps Ryde the final decision-maker, and this ruling is a recommendation only [NS-7]. Profile facts were screened and not used to decide the case: the driver's two upheld no-show disputes in 90 days cannot create a flag without an established breach here, and the rider's clean 90-day history with 0 upheld disputes cannot carry a refund claim by itself [F16][F17][NS-2].

Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint. None contains a threat, intimidation, harassment, a sexual remark or a dangerous-driving allegation — the messages are a pickup notice and a cancellation notice [F9][F10][F12]; no SAFE ground arises [SAFE-1].

rejected_claims.reason: Concedes the very elements that decide the case: the tap at 12:17:10 was 39 m from the pickup and the car stayed within 200 m for 8 min 10 s (490 s) until cancellation, which satisfies NS-1 rather than defeating it [F6][F3][NS-1].

The driver's '8 minutes' wording is read against the record, and both recorded measures reach the 8-minute threshold — 490 s post-tap and a 9 min 55 s arrival-to-cancellation gap — so the timing is compliant with NS-1, not a driver-only count [F6][F5][F10][F12][NS-1].
FARE-1 only strips out unpublished or clause-unsupported add-ons; the $5.00 is the fee the record attaches to this cancellation with a 1.0x multiplier, so nothing is shown to refund [F7][F8][NS-1].

NS-1 turns on the driver's arrival record and the rider's failure to board, not on rider consent; the complete timestamped chat shows an arrival notice at 12:17 with no rider message before the 12:25 cancellation, and the driver's statement is treated as a claim, not as consent [F9][F10][F11][F12][NS-1].

Traffic and weather facts are irrelevant to NS-1, which does not condition the fee on congestion or incidents; no incident near the route and fair weather merely confirm an unobstructed pickup [F13][F14][F15][NS-1].

RD-6 makes a flag available only where the breach is established, and the profile alone cannot decide the case; with NS-1 satisfied there is no established violation to attach a flag to [F17][F16][NS-1][NS-2].

Accepted as far as it goes: the in-app notice at 12:17 and the cancellation message at 12:25 are consistent with the record, but the fee stands on the NS-1 elements, not on the driver's own narrative [F9][F10][F3][NS-1].
Accepted: the timestamped chat and the gapless GPS track settle the wait finding, so no completeness proviso forces human review [F11][F3][NS-1].

The driver's framing of the $5.00 as a waiting fee is set aside — the record labels it a cancellation fee (F4, F7), and NS-6 (boarding plus completed trip) is not the applicable clause; the charge is upheld under NS-1, not NS-6 [F4][F7][F6][NS-1][NS-6].

Accepted only as far as it goes: the driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days cannot decide or support a flag in this case, and his 824 trips and account age do not bear on the fee's validity [F17][F16][NS-2].
